LESSON: WRITING 1.3.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 1 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to write legibly and neatly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication,

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication,

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication.

   Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. trace, model and paint letters of the alphabet in the language,

2. form simple words based on the theme,

3. work jointly to fish sentence cards with the simple words and copy the sentences neatly and legibly,

4. work with peers to fill in blank spaces to complete sentences using vocabulary,

5. display their neatly written sentences on sentence strips in class and conduct gallery walks,

6. take part in a class writing competition focusing on handwriting.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. trace, model and paint letters of the alphabet in the language,
2. form simple words based on the theme,
3. work jointly to fish sentence cards with the simple words and copy the sentences neatly and legibly,
4. work with peers to fill in blank spaces to complete sentences using vocabulary,
5. display their neatly written sentences on sentence strips in class and conduct gallery walks,
6. take part in a class writing competition focusing on handwriting.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.3.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner works with peers to peer review each other’s written

work for improvement during gallery walks.

6

• Learning to Learn: This is developed as the learner builds on their learning when organising and carrying out a class writing

competition focusing on handwriting.

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner works harmoniously with peers to fill in blank spaces to complete sentences.

• Integrity: This is promoted as the learner displays transparency by willingly presenting their own work for peer review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self -esteem: This is promoted as the learner develops confidence in their neat and legible handwriting for effective

communication.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of good handwriting to their learning in Kiswahili and English.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify letters of the alphabet in the language for effective communication,
2. write simple sentences legibly and neatly for written communication,
3. appreciate neatness and legibility in writing for effective communication.

Remember the key question: Why is it important to write legibly and neatly?
